title: Answer API callers without a thread per purchase

blocks.text: This builds on the previous practice: `PaymentEndpoint.java` already contains its solution.

The payment API is moving to a non-blocking web framework. A request handler there must return at once and hand back a `CompletableFuture`, and the framework sends the HTTP response when the future completes. A future that never completes is a caller that hangs until its own client gives up.
Write `handleAsync(...)` in `src/main/java/com/example/practice/PaymentEndpoint.java`. Its callers expect the same statuses as from `handle(...)`, and the same entries on `unknown`. About ten lines.
The tests use the same QMUX and host as before. In some of them the host holds a purchase and answers only when the test lets it.

cases.says: a purchase the host approves completes its future with 200
when no answer comes the listener is called with null, and the future still completes, with 504
a purchase the MUX refuses before sending fails the future with the ISOException and is not an unknown outcome
the listener form does not check the link either, so a down link is answered with 503 before anything is handed to the MUX
the future is returned before the host answers, so no thread is held while the host thinks

origin.section: 4.5 The Asynchronous Form Calls Back Once, With an Answer or With null

concepts: The listener form calls back once, with the answer or with null on expiry, and throws ISOException when it refuses; the caller's future must complete in every case.
